ticket.title: verify falls back to cargo test silently, so a weak receipt is indistinguishable from a configured one
ticket.description:
ALREADY DONE, verified 2026-11-10: the cargo-test fallback is no longer silent. receipts::build prefixes the receipt summary with [fallback: no verification command configured; ran cargo test], appends :cargo-test-fallback to the verifier name, and prints a warning to stderr. Measured live earlier today: SP-49 receipt before its scope was corrected read verifier storypole-verify:cargo-test-fallback with that prefix, and a reader could tell it from a configured run.

RE-CHECKED 2026-11-12 and the claim still holds: receipts.rs:160 appends :cargo-test-fallback to the verifier name, so a fallback run is distinguishable from a configured one in the receipt itself, not only in a console warning.
acceptance_criteria: FIXED 2026-11-06 (storypole commit). No contract change was needed: VerificationReceipt already carries 'command' and 'verifier'. The fallback now states itself three ways - a stderr warning naming the scope
a verifier suffix ':cargo-test-fallback'
and a summary prefix '[fallback: no verification command configured; ran `cargo test`]'. The last one matters most because the receipt is what a later reader trusts
possibly months afterwards.\n\nThe fallback is retained on purpose: cargo is the only tool guaranteed in an individually cloned repo (law 2)
so a weaker default is defensible while an unlabeled one is not.\n\nVerified: fmt clean
clippy -D warnings clean
55/55. NOT verified end-to-end: both the configured and fallback paths need one real 'storypole verify' run
and every repo now has a command configured
so the fallback path needs an unscoped or unconfigured task to exercise.

task.title: verify falls back to cargo test silently, so a weak receipt is indistinguishable from a configured one

acceptance_criteria: ANALYSIS 2026-11-06. ops/verification/mod.rs resolves a command by crate name then repo name via config.verification_command_for()
and falls back to a hardcoded 'cargo test' when neither matches. Nothing records which happened
so a task verified against 'cargo test' alone produces the same shape of receipt as one that ran fmt
clippy
tests and docs. That is the third instance today of the same failure mode - silence that reads as success
alongside outfeed's 'up-to-date' and 'verifier: manual'.\n\nFIX: the receipt must carry the command that actually ran and whether it was configured or a fallback
and verify should say so on stderr when it falls back. Rationale for keeping the fallback rather than erroring: cargo is the only tool guaranteed present in an individually cloned repository (law 2)
and defaulting to a weaker check is defensible; presenting it as equivalent is not.\n\nDo NOT simply error on an unconfigured repo: that would make storypole unusable in a fresh clone
which is the exact scenario the fallback exists for.

FIXED 2026-11-06 (storypole commit). No contract change was needed: VerificationReceipt already carries 'command' and 'verifier'. The fallback now states itself three ways - a stderr warning naming the scope
a verifier suffix ':cargo-test-fallback'
and a summary prefix '[fallback: no verification command configured; ran `cargo test`]'. The last one matters most because the receipt is what a later reader trusts
possibly months afterwards.\n\nThe fallback is retained on purpose: cargo is the only tool guaranteed in an individually cloned repo (law 2)
so a weaker default is defensible while an unlabeled one is not.\n\nVerified: fmt clean
clippy -D warnings clean
55/55. NOT verified end-to-end: both the configured and fallback paths need one real 'storypole verify' run
and every repo now has a command configured
so the fallback path needs an unscoped or unconfigured task to exercise.
